comment: digit zero inside an alpha word is almost always letter o (rec0gnize -> recognize); lexicon-gated
digit one inside an alpha word is usually lowercase l (ana1ysis -> analysis); lexicon-gated
digit one can also be i (1mage -> image); only when l-version is not in lexicon
digit one as capital I; rare in body text; keep for completeness
digit five for letter s (5ample -> sample); lexicon-gated
digit two for letter z (2inc -> zinc); lexicon-gated
digit six for letter b; uncommon in clean scans
digit nine for letter g; uncommon in clean scans
digit eight for letter b (8and -> band); rare
capital I misread inside lowercase words (Iaser -> laser); lexicon-gated
capital O inside lowercase words; risky, keep low
dollar sign for s in degraded scans
at-sign for a in degraded scans
pipe glyph for l or I in degraded scans
rn sequence from letter m (rnetal -> metal); only when result in lexicon; true rn words (barn, kernel) are protected by the original-in-lexicon guard
vv sequence from letter w (vvavelength -> wavelength); lexicon-gated
d can come from cl (daim -> claim); very risky, almost always deferred
cl can come from d in bold fonts; very risky, almost always deferred
three strokes for m in heavy bold or broken fonts
reverse direction (true rn misread as m); rare in machine OCR
ri merged into n in tight kerning
c misread as e (cven -> even) in faded scans
long-s confusion in historical prints (fpectrum -> spectrum)
fi ligature dropped leaving a truncated token (nished -> finished); only when exactly one insertion lands in lexicon
fl ligature dropped; same uniqueness requirement
ff ligature dropped; same uniqueness requirement
ffi ligature dropped; longer insertion, keep medium
spurious space splitting one word in two (diff raction -> diffraction); join must be in lexicon and at least one part unknown
latin a before -particles/-decay/-rays is usually alpha (a-particles -> α-particles)
latin b/B before physics suffix is usually beta; b is also common as a label
capital B before -decay/-emission; ambiguous with boron and magnetic field
latin g before -rays/-radiation is usually gamma
latin y for gamma in some fonts; rare
symbol-mash token that no lexicon word can explain; mark, never guess
standalone lowercase l next to a number or unit (l mV) may be digit 1 or litre; genuinely ambiguous, always deferred
standalone capital I in numeric context may be digit 1 or pronoun
standalone capital O in numeric context may be digit zero
